title: Large-scale LoRaWAN deployments become easier through QR codes and relays
summary: LoRaWAN devices typically require users to enter parameters such as the DevEUI, JoinEUI (formerly AppEUI), AppKey, and potentially the DevAddr plus the session keys, depending on the activation mode (ABP vs OTAA). This is manageable for a handful of devices, but becomes time-consuming, error-prone, and costly at scale. To make the onboarding process easier and scale LoRaWAN networks more effectively, the LoRa Alliance has now introduced three new documents: the TS014 and TS018 specifications and the TR016 technical recommendations. They should all help users get a device onto a network quickly, securely, and with minimal manual work, such as scanning a QR code. Here are the links and summaries for all three documents: TS014-1.0.0 LoRaWAN End-Device Capabilities API Specification TS014 eliminates manual data entry and proprietary workarounds by enabling LoRaWAN networks to automatically pull device profiles. title: CtrlVibe AI Console keypad An OpenAI Codex Micro alternative for AI workflows (Crowdfunding)
summary: The CtrlVibe AI Console is a programmable desktop keypad designed for AI workflows. The device includes hardware controls for switching between AI tools, launching shortcuts, selecting execution modes, and recording voice input. It comes with nine programmable mechanical keys, a rotary encoder, a three-position switch, a 1.14-inch LCD, a built-in MEMS microphone, USB-C and Bluetooth connectivity, and RGB status lighting. The features and specifications of the CtrlVibe make it an alternative to Work Louder Codex Micro, a $230 mechanical macropad designed for OpenAI Codex. There is also an open-source firmware project available for the M5Stack Core2 that reproduces many of the Codex Micro s features. While the Codex Micro is designed specifically for OpenAI Codex, the CtrlVibe AI Console can be used with multiple AI tools and uses a rotary encoder to switch between applications or models, along with a three-position hardware switch for selecting AI execution modes.
